open_points.subject: canonical security-review grammar authority
open_points.text:
The record follows the Workbench's canonical security-review grammar, a design
fact of authoring that no generated code reads
open_points.question: Which identifiable Workbench grammar revision governs this accepted review, and can a later grammar revision change whether the unchanged review passes?
options: Freeze the grammar revision used when A21 is accepted.
Use the grammar supplied by the Workbench checkout that later runs design_lint.
Require an explicit migration and renewed acceptance before a newer grammar applies.
open_points.default_guess: Freeze and record the grammar revision used when A21 is accepted.

witness.initial: A21 is accepted with the nine listed categories under Workbench grammar revision W1.
events: The Workbench is upgraded to revision W2, which adds a required security-review category.
An author runs design_lint --state 2 without changing A21.
outcomes: The review still passes because acceptance pinned W1.
The review fails because design_lint applies W2 to the unchanged record.
witness.observer: The author attempting to proceed to State 3.

open_points.subject: admissible reference combinations in a security-review outcome
open_points.question: Are the locally stated reference conditions exhaustive, or does the unnamed canonical grammar impose additional restrictions such as forbidding non-decision references alongside the required decision on an APPLICABLE category?
options: Permit any indexed references, provided every reference resolves and each outcome has its stated required evidence.
Permit only the reference kinds allowed for that outcome by an identified canonical grammar revision.
State the complete allowed and forbidden reference combinations directly in A21.
open_points.default_guess: Permit additional indexed references because APPLICABLE requires at least one accepted decision rather than only accepted decisions, while still requiring every reference to resolve.

witness.initial: An APPLICABLE category references accepted decision A16 and indexed model M27.
events: One careful gate implementer applies the explicit rule that the category references at least one accepted decision and that every reference resolves.
Another applies an assumed canonical-grammar restriction that APPLICABLE references may contain decisions only.
outcomes: The record passes because A16 satisfies the minimum and M27 resolves.
The record fails because M27 is not an accepted decision.
witness.observer: The review author and the State 3 gate.

set_aside.subject: required security-review categories
set_aside.question: What is the exact closed set of required category names: precisely the nine entries in this Security review, or a separately defined Workbench set that may contain other names?
options: The nine category names listed in A21 are the complete closed set.
A separately versioned Workbench grammar supplies the complete closed set.
A21 must enumerate the set and require it to equal a named Workbench grammar revision.
set_aside.default_guess: Treat the nine listed category names as the closed set and require an explicit A21 change to alter it.

witness.initial: The record contains exactly the nine categories printed in A21 and no other category.
events: A careful implementer builds the State 2 gate from the nine entries in the review.
Another careful implementer treats the unnamed Workbench grammar as authoritative and includes an additional required category.
Both validate the same unchanged record.
outcomes: The record passes because every one of the nine listed categories occurs exactly once.
The record fails because the additional grammar-defined category is missing.
witness.observer: The author waiting for State 3 to become unblocked.

set_aside.set_aside_because: an unchanged passage of a unit reviewed for its change
